title: Product lower bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers
statement:
For positive integers $k$ and $l$, write $r(a,b)$ for the Ramsey number: the least $n$ such that every simple graph on $n$ vertices contains either a clique on $a$ vertices or an independent set of $b$ vertices. Then, provided $k \ge 1$ and $l \ge 1$,
\[
\bigl(r(k+1,\,k+1) - 1\bigr)\bigl(r(l+1,\,l+1) - 1\bigr) + 1 \;\le\; r(kl+1,\,kl+1).
\]
hypotheses_covered: conclusion: product of (r(k+1,k+1)-1) and (r(l+1,l+1)-1), plus 1, bounds r(kl+1,kl+1) from below
